evals.name: purchase-invoice-amount-drift-cross-repo
evals.prompt: our purchase invoice totals keep drifting when someone changes the ledger account on a line — the invoice ends up worth less than the supplier actually billed. i genuinely don't understand where these amounts even get calculated. is it in the blazor frontend or in the api? it's a black box to me. can you explain the whole flow, from the AI reading the PDF through to the journal posting, and tell me where the problem actually is?
evals.expected_output: A published artifact explaining that the arithmetic lives in a shared library both sides call, that the caller chooses the split direction, and that splitting from net makes the gross an output — traced through the header total to the journal's supplier row, with diagrams and real file paths.
evals.notes: Requires three repos on disk: a Blazor frontend, a .NET backend, and an AI extraction service. The point of this case is that the answer spans all three and the naive answer picks one side.
assertions: Published a Claude artifact and returned its URL
Answered the user's literal question: the arithmetic is neither frontend nor backend, it is a shared library both sides call
Reached all three repositories, not only the frontend
Stated where code executes, distinguishing the browser from the server
Separated the code that computes from the code that chooses the direction of the split
Identified the mechanism: splitting from net makes the gross an output
Traced the consequence through the header total to the journal's supplier row
Cited concrete file paths that exist in the repositories
Told the user the artifact is private and needs sharing

evals.name: embedded-mixed-depth
evals.prompt: You are called by wsbaser:review in embedded mode. The record is at evals/files/review-decided.json and has reached stage decided; work against that file. It holds three issues: issue 1 is a one-line issue (a log message says 'Retrying' where the code gives up); issue 2 is a race condition, two requests that save the same estimate concurrently so one update to the total is lost; issue 3 is a UI question with two options for what a user without permission sees on the estimate page. Write the explanation for every issue, and option blocks where choosing needs them, then hand the record back.
evals.expected_output: Three explanations of clearly different length and form: one sentence for issue 1; for issue 2 the background, a picture of both orderings including the failing one, and the code with file:line; for issue 3 the current screen first and option blocks that show what each option produces. The record passes check_record.py --stage ready, and no fold holds fewer than 600 characters.

evals.name: short-question-stays-short
evals.prompt: quick one: which file sets the default page size for the invoice list?
evals.expected_output: A terminal answer of a few lines naming the file with file:line and the value. No artifact is published.

evals.name: reviewer-claim
evals.prompt: a reviewer left this on my PR: "UserStore.Find can return null here and there is no test covering it, so this will blow up in production." is he right? explain.
evals.expected_output: The answer quotes the comment, splits it into its separate claims (can return null, no test, will fail in production) with a verdict and evidence for each, and shows the relevant code with file:line in the sentence before it.
